# `task_route`

**Task Route.** Send a task back to its router: ``aq task route`` (spec §7).

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Capability | `task_route` |
| Side effect | `composite` |
| Idempotency | none |
| Retry safe | no |
| Timeout | none |
| Preview | not supported |
| Defined in | [`src/commands/contracts/generated.py`](../../../src/commands/contracts/generated.py) |
| Contract fingerprint | `sha256:73f77274dbc2d72075bc21fb853ccd0321eb4c3d097bf4bca1e8bd48a0275ba0` |

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `task_id` | `string` | yes | — | Task ID to re-route |
| `intelligence_class` | `string` | no | — | New intelligence-class hint for the router (e.g. 'fast-high', 'standard-high', 'deep-high'); the router honours it within its policy's bounds for the kind. Omit to keep the task's hint; an empty value clears it. |
| `task_type` | `string` | no | — | New kind for the router (e.g. 'feature', 'bugfix', 'design', 'docs'). Omit to keep the task's kind; an empty value clears it. |
| `prefer` | `string` | no | — | Routing preference for the router to weigh before scoring: a harness id (e.g. 'codex') or a worker profile id. The router still picks the route; this only decides whether it may route elsewhere. Omit to keep the task's preference; an empty value clears it. An unknown name, a disabled profile and a non-worker profile are refused. |
| `prefer_mode` | `"soft" \| "strict"` | no | `"soft"` | How the router may refuse 'prefer': 'soft' (default) routes to it when it has headroom and routes normally when it does not; 'strict' admits only that harness or profile and holds the task rather than falling back to another one. On 'aq task route' a mode with no 'prefer' keeps the stored target. |
| `reason` | `string` | no | — | Why the task is re-routed; posted as a task comment. |
